text: default, [get_prm()] treats every diagonal omega log-normal reports CV% accordingly: IIVCL IIVV get cv column; -diagonal fixed-effect rows don’t (CV% defined diagonal random effect acting specific structural parameter). already CV% ’d get hand log-normal assumption – add_prm_association() becomes useful moment assumption wrong given parameter. Say CL actually fit logit-normal instead (purely illustration – wasn’t, model). Declaring changes cv column; nothing else fit table shape changes: Built-distributions cover common cases: log (default, made explicit), logexp (log(1+X)), logit, arcsin, nmboxcox (Box-Cox, needs lambda): anything else, custom() takes qdist/pdist pair (transform inverse): Redeclaring association parameter replaces ; drop_prm_association() removes entirely (falling back log-normal default): One important caveat: CV% calculation assumes fixed-effect value natural, untransformed scale. CL actually fitted logit scale (just related logit-normal omega), reported value need converting back first – see Rescaling mutate_prm() .

title: Parameter Associations: Omega CVs and Covariate Effects
text: Six built-ins cover usual covariate models, constructed effect ratio exactly 1 ref regardless theta value: Note differently power linear read THETA7: power exponent 0.007 barely moves ratio across realistic CLCR range, number linear slope gives substantial swing. Picking right built-covariate actually enters model matters – computation can’t tell two apart , mismatched builtin produces numerically valid silently wrong ratio. none built-ins fit, custom() takes fun(cov, ref, theta), validated declaration time confirm fun(ref, ref, theta) == 1 probe thetas: drop_cov_association() removes declared (parameter, covariate) pair, way drop_prm_association() works omegas:
code: # power (allometric): (COV/ref)^theta xpdb_x %>% add_cov_association(TVCL ~ power(CLCR, THETA7, ref = 64)) %>% prm_contcov() #> # A tibble: 3 × 10 #>   param covariate covtype level value is_ref effect ci_low ci_high ci_method  #> * <chr> <chr>     <chr>   <chr> <chr> <lgl>   <dbl>  <dbl>   <dbl> <chr>      #> 1 TVCL  CLCR      cont    low   40    FALSE   0.997  0.995   0.998 simulation #> 2 TVCL  CLCR      cont    ref   64    TRUE    1      1       1     simulation #> 3 TVCL  CLCR      cont    high  102   FALSE   1.00   1.00    1.00  simulation #> # `effect` is a ratio to the parameter's typical value (1 at the reference #> covariate value/level); CI via simulation.  # exponential: exp(theta*(COV-ref)) xpdb_x %>% add_cov_association(TVCL ~ exponential(CLCR, THETA7, ref = 64)) %>% prm_contcov() #> # A tibble: 3 × 10 #>   param covariate covtype level value is_ref effect ci_low ci_high ci_method  #> * <chr> <chr>     <chr>   <chr> <chr> <lgl>   <dbl>  <dbl>   <dbl> <chr>      #> 1 TVCL  CLCR      cont    low   40    FALSE   0.842  0.776   0.917 simulation #> 2 TVCL  CLCR      cont    ref   64    TRUE    1      1       1     simulation #> 3 TVCL  CLCR      cont    high  102   FALSE   1.31   1.15    1.49  simulation #> # `effect` is a ratio to the parameter's typical value (1 at the reference #> covariate value/level); CI via simulation.  # additive: (theta+COV)/(theta+ref) -- an uncommon but simple par = theta + cov model xpdb_x %>% add_cov_association(TVCL ~ additive(CLCR, THETA7, ref = 64)) %>% prm_contcov() #> # A tibble: 3 × 10 #>   param covariate covtype level value is_ref effect ci_low ci_high ci_method  #> * <chr> <chr>     <chr>   <chr> <chr> <lgl>   <dbl>  <dbl>   <dbl> <chr>      #> 1 TVCL  CLCR      cont    low   40    FALSE   0.625  0.625   0.625 simulation #> 2 TVCL  CLCR      cont    ref   64    TRUE    1      1       1     simulation #> 3 TVCL  CLCR      cont    high  102   FALSE   1.59   1.59    1.59  simulation #> # `effect` is a ratio to the parameter's typical value (1 at the reference #> covariate value/level); CI via simulation.  # hockey-stick (PsN-style): different slope above/below ref (which doubles as the # breakpoint by default; see `brk=` to separate them) xpdb_x %>% add_cov_association(TVCL ~ hockey(CLCR, THETA7, THETA4, ref = 64)) %>% prm_contcov() #> # A tibble: 3 × 10 #>   param covariate covtype level value is_ref effect ci_low ci_high ci_method  #> * <chr> <chr>     <chr>   <chr> <chr> <lgl>   <dbl>  <dbl>   <dbl> <chr>      #> 1 TVCL  CLCR      cont    low   40    FALSE   0.828  0.747   0.913 simulation #> 2 TVCL  CLCR      cont    ref   64    TRUE    1      1       1     simulation #> 3 TVCL  CLCR      cont    high  102   FALSE   8.90   7.68   10.1   simulation #> # `effect` is a ratio to the parameter's typical value (1 at the reference #> covariate value/level); CI via simulation.  # catshift: one theta per non-reference categorical level xpdb_x %>% add_cov_association(TVCL ~ catshift(SEX, THETA4, ref = 1)) %>% prm_catcov() #> # A tibble: 2 × 10 #>   param covariate covtype level value is_ref effect ci_low ci_high ci_method  #> * <chr> <chr>     <chr>   <chr> <chr> <lgl>   <dbl>  <dbl>   <dbl> <chr>      #> 1 TVCL  SEX       cat     1     1     TRUE     1      1       1    simulation #> 2 TVCL  SEX       cat     2     2     FALSE    1.21   1.18    1.24 simulation #> # `effect` is a ratio to the parameter's typical value (1 at the reference #> covariate value/level); CI via simulation. xpdb_x %>%   add_cov_association(     TVCL ~ custom(CLCR, THETA7, ref = 64, fun = function(cov, ref, theta) (cov / ref)^theta)   ) %>%   prm_contcov() #> # A tibble: 3 × 10 #>   param covariate covtype level value is_ref effect ci_low ci_high ci_method  #> * <chr> <chr>     <chr>   <chr> <chr> <lgl>   <dbl>  <dbl>   <dbl> <chr>      #> 1 TVCL  CLCR      cont    low   40    FALSE   0.997  0.995   0.998 simulation #> 2 TVCL  CLCR      cont    ref   64    TRUE    1      1       1     simulation #> 3 TVCL  CLCR      cont    high  102   FALSE   1.00   1.00    1.00  simulation #> # `effect` is a ratio to the parameter's typical value (1 at the reference #> covariate value/level); CI via simulation. xpdb_x %>%   add_cov_association(TVCL ~ linear(CLCR, THETA7, ref = 64)) %>%   drop_cov_association(TVCL ~ CLCR) %>%   prm_cov() #> # A tibble: 0 × 10 #> # ℹ 10 variables: param <chr>, covariate <chr>, covtype <chr>, level <chr>, #> #   value <chr>, is_ref <lgl>, effect <dbl>, ci_low <dbl>, ci_high <dbl>, #> #   ci_method <chr>

title: Describe parameter/covariate associations — add_cov_association
text: Format associations : LHS ~ fun(COVARIATE, THETA..., ref = ..., ...) LHS: Selector fixed-effect (theta) parameter, exactly add_prm_association() ({m}, {name} {label}, unquoted). Multiple parameters can share one association + (eg, covariate affects CL Q theta). RHS COVARIATE: first (positional) argument. bare, unquoted name contcov/catcov column (see xpose::xp_var()) – fixed-effect omega selector. RHS THETA...: One positional arguments, selecting fixed-effect parameter(s) carry covariate effect magnitude (selector rules LHS – {m}/{name}/ {label}, unquoted). many expected depends fun; see built-list . RHS ref: Required, named, default, every association regardless fun. covariate value (continuous covariates) raw level (categorical covariates) effect normalized – point reported effect ratio exactly 1. way safely infer xpdb alone (NONMEM control streams commonly normalize covariate hardcoded constant baked code, invisible xpose), must always stated explicitly, way add_prm_association()'s nmboxcox requires explicit lambda. built-ins express covariate's effect multiplicative effect_ratio parameter's typical value, constructed effect_ratio == 1 whenever covariate equals ref, regardless theta value. Available built-ins: linear(COV, THETA, ref=): \(1 + \theta (COV - ref)\) power(COV, THETA, ref=): \((COV / ref)^\theta\) (allometric) exponential(COV, THETA, ref=): \(e^{\theta (COV - ref)}\) additive(COV, THETA, ref=): \((\theta + COV) / (\theta + ref)\). uncommon simple form covariate added directly (implicit coefficient 1, unlike linear's explicit slope) intercept-like THETA, eg CL = THETA(n) + WT underlying model. hockey(COV, THETA_LO, THETA_HI, ref=, brk=ref): PsN's "hockey-stick" two-slope piecewise-linear model – \(1 + \theta_{lo} (COV - ref)\) COV <= brk, \(1 + \theta_{hi} (COV - ref)\) COV > brk. brk (breakpoint) defaults ref (PsN's usual default: breakpoint = normalization reference), can given separately, eg covariate normalized observed median clinically meaningful cutpoint round number (ref = 90, brk = 60 eGFR-like covariate). catshift(COV, THETA..., ref=): One theta per non-reference raw level categorical covariate, effect_ratio = 1 + THETA_i level (1 ref). Assumes typical NONMEM pattern one theta per non-reference category (eg (RACE.EQ.2) CLCOV = THETA(9)). Thetas matched non-reference levels ascending raw-value order – order ambiguous wrong given model, use custom() instead. anything else, custom(COV, THETA..., ref=, fun=) escape hatch: fun function (cov, ref, theta) (theta always numeric vector, even one THETA selector given) returning effect ratio. custom() verified construction way built-ins can, add_cov_association() validates declaration time evaluating fun(ref, ref, theta) probe values theta (currently-fitted value, coincidentally pass fun still wrong theta values) requires equal 1; , error states required invariant shows fun actually returned, rather failing silently much later plotting.

code: # xpdb_x's THETA7 ("CRCL on CL") is a genuine covariate effect already # in the model, so this is a faithful (if allometric-flavored, for # illustration) description of it: xpdb_x %>%   add_cov_association(TVCL ~ power(CLCR, THETA7, ref = 64)) %>%   prm_cov() #> # A tibble: 3 × 10 #>   param covariate covtype level value is_ref effect ci_low ci_high ci_method  #>   <chr> <chr>     <chr>   <chr> <chr> <lgl>   <dbl>  <dbl>   <dbl> <chr>      #> 1 TVCL  CLCR      cont    low   40    FALSE   0.997  0.995   0.998 simulation #> 2 TVCL  CLCR      cont    ref   64    TRUE    1      1       1     simulation #> 3 TVCL  CLCR      cont    high  102   FALSE   1.00   1.00    1.00  simulation #> # `effect` is a ratio to the parameter's typical value (1 at the reference #> covariate value/level); CI via simulation.  # hockey-stick (PsN-style): different slope above/below the reference xpdb_x %>%   add_cov_association(TVCL ~ hockey(CLCR, THETA7, THETA4, ref = 64)) %>%   prm_cov() #> # A tibble: 3 × 10 #>   param covariate covtype level value is_ref effect ci_low ci_high ci_method  #>   <chr> <chr>     <chr>   <chr> <chr> <lgl>   <dbl>  <dbl>   <dbl> <chr>      #> 1 TVCL  CLCR      cont    low   40    FALSE   0.828  0.747   0.913 simulation #> 2 TVCL  CLCR      cont    ref   64    TRUE    1      1       1     simulation #> 3 TVCL  CLCR      cont    high  102   FALSE   8.90   7.68   10.1   simulation #> # `effect` is a ratio to the parameter's typical value (1 at the reference #> covariate value/level); CI via simulation.  # Categorical: one theta per non-reference level. SEX has 2 levels # (1, 2), so catshift needs exactly one theta for the non-reference # level; THETA4 is reused here purely for illustration. xpdb_x %>%   add_cov_association(TVCL ~ catshift(SEX, THETA4, ref = 1)) %>%   prm_cov() #> # A tibble: 2 × 10 #>   param covariate covtype level value is_ref effect ci_low ci_high ci_method  #>   <chr> <chr>     <chr>   <chr> <chr> <lgl>   <dbl>  <dbl>   <dbl> <chr>      #> 1 TVCL  SEX       cat     1     1     TRUE     1      1       1    simulation #> 2 TVCL  SEX       cat     2     2     FALSE    1.21   1.18    1.24 simulation #> # `effect` is a ratio to the parameter's typical value (1 at the reference #> covariate value/level); CI via simulation.  # custom(): fun(cov, ref, theta) must equal 1 when cov == ref xpdb_x %>%   add_cov_association(     TVCL ~ custom(CLCR, THETA7, ref = 64,                 fun = function(cov, ref, theta) (cov/ref)^theta)   ) %>%   prm_cov() #> # A tibble: 3 × 10 #>   param covariate covtype level value is_ref effect ci_low ci_high ci_method  #>   <chr> <chr>     <chr>   <chr> <chr> <lgl>   <dbl>  <dbl>   <dbl> <chr>      #> 1 TVCL  CLCR      cont    low   40    FALSE   0.997  0.995   0.998 simulation #> 2 TVCL  CLCR      cont    ref   64    TRUE    1      1       1     simulation #> 3 TVCL  CLCR      cont    high  102   FALSE   1.00   1.00    1.00  simulation #> # `effect` is a ratio to the parameter's typical value (1 at the reference #> covariate value/level); CI via simulation.  # Dropping an association is easy bad_assoc <- xpdb_x %>%   add_cov_association(TVCL ~ power(CLCR, THETA7, ref = 64)) bad_assoc %>%   drop_cov_association(TVCL ~ CLCR) %>%   prm_cov() #> # A tibble: 0 × 10 #> # ℹ 10 variables: param <chr>, covariate <chr>, covtype <chr>, level <chr>, #> #   value <chr>, is_ref <lgl>, effect <dbl>, ci_low <dbl>, ci_high <dbl>, #> #   ci_method <chr>

title: Add, apply, list, amend or remove xpdb processing presets — add_process_preset
text: "process preset" one-sided formula (using .x incoming xpdb, purrr-style lambda) plain function bundles repeated processing pipeline – e.g. converting xp_xtras, dropping unused ETAs, assigning labels/levels – can re-applied process_preset() instead retyped every model. add_process_preset() stores preset current session (name, auto-incrementing integer name given). process_preset() applies stored preset xpdb. print_process_preset() lists stored presets. remove_process_preset() deletes one. amend_process_preset() replaces existing preset's definition place.

title: Add, apply, list, amend or remove xpdb processing presets — add_process_preset
text: default, presets session-: vanish R restarts. Set persist = TRUE additionally write current set presets .Rprofile recreated automatically future sessions. Per CRAN policy, package must write files outside tempdir() without user's explicit, interactive consent, never side effect non-interactive process (R CMD check, tests, vignette builds, Rscript, ...). Accordingly, persist = TRUE: ever writes rlang::is_interactive() TRUE – errors otherwise, always -op R CMD check/testthat/ knitr – asks confirmation (via utils::askYesNo()) writing, unless ask = FALSE passed explicitly (already-interactive) caller. target file defaults project-scoped .Rprofile (getwd()), affects R sessions started directory; pass profile = "user" instead target user-level profile (Sys.getenv("R_PROFILE_USER"), falling back ~/.Rprofile), string use literal file path. Presets written single marked block (bounded # >>> xpose.xtras process presets ... >>> / # <<< ... <<<) re-syncing replaces whole block rather accumulating duplicate calls, block removed entirely last preset deleted. Persisted presets must self-contained – since recreated deparsed source new session, depend transient local variables session created .

Defaults . .problem <numeric> Problem number. .subprob <numeric> Subprob number. .method <numeric> Method. ci_method <character> "simulation" (default) draws nsim samples theta N(theta_hat, se) (mirrors mutate_prm()'s .autose approach) propagates (possibly nonlinear) effect_ratio function, taking resulting sample quantiles interval; accurate strongly nonlinear forms (power, exponential, hockey). "delta" first-order analytic (numerical-gradient) log-scale approximation – cheap deterministic, less accurate nonlinear association . treat multiple thetas (eg hockey, multi-level catshift) independent, ignoring covariance . probs <numeric(2)> prm_contcov(): quantiles covariate's observed data used "low"/"high" evaluation points. level <numeric> Confidence level effect interval. nsim <numeric> Number simulation draws, ci_method = "simulation". keep_draws <logical> TRUE (requires ci_method = "simulation"), attach draws list-column: raw nsim simulated effect-ratio draws behind row's CI. code: if (requireNamespace("bbr", quietly = TRUE)) {   # Build a bbr-style model directory from the bundled pheno_saemimp example   src_dir <- system.file("pheno_saemimp", package = "xpose.xtras")   mod_dir <- tempfile("xp_from_bbr_ex")   dir.create(mod_dir)   file.copy(file.path(src_dir, "run18.mod"), file.path(mod_dir, "18.mod"))   out_dir <- file.path(mod_dir, "18")   dir.create(out_dir)   out_files <- setdiff(list.files(src_dir, pattern = "^run18\\."), "run18.mod")   for (f in out_files) {     file.copy(       file.path(src_dir, f),       file.path(out_dir, paste0("18.", sub("^run18\\.", "", f)))     )   }   # bbr considers a run finished once bbi has written this file   writeLines("{}", file.path(out_dir, "bbi_config.json"))    mod <- bbr::new_model(file.path(mod_dir, "18"), .description = "Phenobarbital SAEM model")   print(xp_from_bbr(mod))   unlink(mod_dir, recursive = TRUE) } #> Warning: No table files could be found. #>  #> ── ~ xp_xtras object  #> Model description: Phenobarbital SAEM model #> 18.lst overview:  #>  - Software: nonmem 7.5.0  #>  - Attached files (memory usage 348.5 Kb):  #>    + obs tabs: <none>  #>    + sim tabs: <none>  #>    + output files: 18.cor, 18.cov, 18.ext, 18.phi, 18.shk  #>    + special: <none>  #>  - gg_theme: theme_readable  #>  - xp_theme: xp_xtra_theme new_x$xp_theme  #>  - Options: dir = /tmp/Rtmp9mG6BR/xp_from_bbr_ex1be851b3a2bd/18, quiet = TRUE, manual_import = NULL, cvtype = exact

code: data("xpdb_ex_pk", package = "xpose")  # Arbitrary copy xpdb_ex_pk2 <- xpdb_ex_pk  # Simplest call set1 <- xpose_set(xpdb_ex_pk, xpdb_ex_pk2)  # With predefined relationships set2 <- xpose_set(xpdb_ex_pk, xpdb_ex_pk2,   .relationships = list(xpdb_ex_pk2 ~ xpdb_ex_pk)   )  # Alternative predefined relationships set2b <- xpose_set(xpdb_ex_pk, xpdb_ex_pk2,   .as_ordered = TRUE   )  # With custom labels set3 <- xpose_set(mod1 = xpdb_ex_pk, mod2 = xpdb_ex_pk2,   .relationships = list(mod2 ~ mod1)   )  # Alternative set3 using dyanmic dots mod_list <- list(   mod1 = xpdb_ex_pk,   mod2 = xpdb_ex_pk2 ) mod_rels <- list(   mod2 ~ mod1 ) set3b = xpose_set(!!!mod_list, .relationships = mod_rels)

title: xpose.xtras 0.2.2
text: Added xtras_data(), wrapper around xpose::xpose_data() %>% as_xp_xtras() silences rlang_warning-batched chatter readr/dplyr can raise parsing tables NaN/Inf otherwise oddly formatted values, without hiding warnings indicate actual read failure. xp_from_bbr() now uses internally. (#77) Added recalc_shk(), recalculates eta shrinkage directly individual estimates rather parsing NONMEM’s reported value, .etastype argument exclude “true zero” (opposed merely near-zero) etas calculation. Etas matched omega column name possible (eg nlmixr2 models), falling back NONMEM’s ETA<k>/OMEGA(k,k) numbering convention. (#79) Added new shk variable type, plus derive_shk()/backfill_shk() populate : per-individual eta shrinkage contribution diagnostic (log((eta - mean(eta))^2)). (#78) Added shk_grid()/shk_vs_cov_grid()/shk_vs_contcov()/ shk_vs_catcov(), mirroring eta_grid()/eta_vs_cov_grid()/ eta_vs_contcov()/eta_vs_catcov() new shk diagnostic. (#78) Added list = FALSE eta_vs_contcov()/eta_vs_catcov()/ shk_vs_contcov()/shk_vs_catcov(), combining per-variable plots onto one shared, faceted plot instead list, paginating 9 panels per page. (#82) Added covvar eta_vs_contcov()/eta_vs_catcov()/ shk_vs_contcov()/shk_vs_catcov() select specific covariates, mirroring etavar/shkvar; also added cols alias eta_vs_cov_grid()/shk_vs_cov_grid(). (#82) Added normalize_etas()/normalise_etas(), set top-level xpdb$normalize_etas slot (like $covs, see add_cov_association() – xpdb$options entry, settable via set_option()) dividing eta omega-implied SD (, .use_sd = TRUE, empirical SD individual estimates) eta_grid()/ eta_vs_cov_grid()/eta_vs_contcov()/eta_vs_catcov() – underlying data never modified. (#81)

title: xpose.xtras 0.2.2
text: nlmixr2_as_xtra() now reports rejected object’s class xpose.nlmixr2::xpose_data_nlmixr2() doesn’t recognize nlmixr2 fit, instead generic upstream message. backfill_iofv() now gives clear error called without xpdb instead cryptic cli formatting failure. (#84) Fixed print.xpose_data()/print.xp_xtras() erroring instead printing whenever xpdb$options entry multi-element list (eg default_labs/default_watermark one key set). (#81) Fixed critical bug xpdb$foo <- value/xpdb[["foo"]] <- value (including inside patch_condn(), run automatically as_xpdb_x()) silently strip xp_xtras/xpose_data classes ggplot2 versions 4.0, due class-name collision ggplot2’s internal aes() mapping class. (#74) conflicted now optional (Suggests) dependency instead hard requirement, consulted user loaded . Package startup longer prints “Registered S3 method overwritten” notice print.xpose_plot, reminder attach xpose now also names load-order-sensitive bugfix stake. (#72) irep() longer deprecated favor xpose::irep() xpose >= 0.5.0: xpose reverted upstream fix, package’s version needed regardless installed xpose version. catdv_vs_ipred() longer triggers spurious ggplot2 lifecycle warning (incorrectly blaming xpose) mapping size line layer, ’s deprecated favor linewidth. (#75) set_var_types_x() longer mistypes columns tidyselect expression matches 10+ columns one type (e.g. eta = matches(...)), one type name prefix another (e.g. id/idv). (#76)

title: xpose.xtras 0.2.0
text: xp_from_bbr() converts ‘bbr’ model directly xp_xtras object. New parameter/covariate association system (add_cov_association(), prm_cov() family) xplot_forest() / cov_forest() visualization; see new parameter-associations vignette. cormat() visualizes parameter correlation/covariance matrix, NONMEM nlmixr2 models. catdv_vs_occ() catdv_vs_ipred() add categorical DV diagnostic plots (observed-vs-predicted trend across occasions, binned calibration). left_join_x() backfills missing variables xpdb via coalescing left join. Default label overrides, plot watermarking, flexible save wrapper (set_default_labs(), add_watermark(), ggsave_xp()), configurable via set_xtras_options() auto-applied print/save. See new plot-output vignette. patch_condn() corrects ‘xpose’s condition number calculation multi-method NONMEM runs, applied automatically byas_xpdb_x()`. focus_function() / focus_qapply() now support output-generating functions (plots, tables), just xpdb-transforming ones. New logLik(), AIC(), BIC() methods xpose_data xpose_set objects. ind_plots_sample() plots representative (optionally stratified) sample individuals instead whole dataset. plot.xpose_data() runs configurable batch diagnostic plots one call. process_preset() family saves replays reusable xpdb processing pipeline name, optionally persisted across sessions.

title: xpose.xtras 0.2.0
text: set_dv_probs() longer crashes .problem omitted. conflicted preferences now re-applied regardless package attach order, fixing spurious “found 2 packages” errors. Fixed inconsistent ‘cli’ message coloring caused color-formatting helper evaluated install time instead call time. Fixed title/description typo %p%. Fixed misleading default subtitle/caption labels model-averaged plots, previously reported statistics just one averaged models. Fixed as_xpdb_x() / check_xpdb_x() erroring xpose_data objects table data. Fixed xplot_pairs() silently ignoring custom catcont_opts$other_fun, removed unreachable leftover duplicate-axis-label block roc_by_mod().
